correctness.rationale: PASS. The derivative 3a_i x_i^2 in characteristic seven proves smoothness for all nonzero diagonal coefficients. The diagonal Hessian determinant is proportional to the product of the five coordinates, so projective linear equivalences preserve the five hyperplanes, hence are monomial; scalar/cube-class permutation reduces all coefficient vectors to precisely seven classes. Every F7-rational line in P4 has a unique echelon-reduced two-vector spanning matrix; checking all 140050 2-planes gives the full (points,line-degrees) table. An independent enumeration of every echelon line, its eight normalized F7 points and all seven test cubics reproduced point totals [435,477,288,309,414,498,393], line totals [135,189,27,27,81,270,36], and the exact seven local-degree histograms. The separate source algorithm based on the two mixed cubic polar equations gives an additional independently coded pointwise check. All seven rows obey sum(m_j)=number of points and sum(j m_j)=8 times number of lines. Enumeration exactly covers finite F7 linear incidence, not all smooth cubics or fields.

value.rationale: PASS. Rational lines and their incidence through individual rational points on smooth cubic threefolds over the challenging small field F7 are natural geometric invariants. The seven diagonal cubic twists form a canonical closed family, not arbitrarily hand-selected equations. Exact local profiles show three classes where all points lie on rational lines, four with 189/135/135/162 uncovered points, and a pair of 27-line classes with different incidence geometry. This complete classification is strictly richer than a sample or a total-line census while not purporting to solve the arbitrary-cubic existence problem.
